source.quote: LUMIN's own page for the S2, read 2026-11-24. Network playback: « Up to DSD512 »; « Up to 384 kHz, 16-32-bit, Stereo ». Digital INPUTS: « OPTICAL/Coaxial: » « PCM 44.1 kHz-192 kHz, 16-24-bit » / « DSD64 (DoP64, DSD over PCM) »; also « 2x SPDIF » « DoP64 / 192 kHz 24-bit compatible ». Digital outputs: USB « Native DSD512 support » / « PCM 44.1-384 kHz, 16-32-bit, Stereo ». Converter: « Dual ESS SABRE32 ES9038Pro DAC chips ». Processing: « DSD256 upsampling option for all files »; « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files »; « MQA QRONO d2a filters available for all PCM music (excluding via AirPlay) ». Footer and legal as on the X2 page; no prohibition.

facts.chip: « Dual ESS SABRE32 ES9038Pro DAC chips ».

device_settings.why: The page offers « DSD256 upsampling option for all files » and « PCM 384kHz upsampling option for all files ». Left OFF: Auto's whole purpose is to choose the format and rate reaching the conversion stage, and a device-side resampler would redo that work with a filter we did not design and cannot account for. Turn it on only for a listener who prefers it and is not using Auto. Same reasoning as FiiO's « All to DSD ».

_les_filtres_MQA_QRONO_sont_nommes_et_co: « MQA QRONO d2a filters available for all PCM music (excluding via AirPlay) ». A NAMED filter - QRONO d2a - offered for all PCM, not only for MQA material, and withdrawn on one transport. No device_settings entry is written: the page never says how to select it or what it does to the signal, and a filter whose effect is undocumented cannot be recommended. It is the sixteenth filter name collected in two days and the first whose availability depends on which protocol the music arrived over.
_le_plafond_reseau_depasse_le_plafond_de: « Up to DSD512 » over the network against « DSD64 (DoP64) » on optical and coaxial - eight times - and 384 kHz against 192 kHz. The device figure is the network figure, and the two physical inputs are far below it. The network path has no key in the interface vocabulary, so this record shows a device that does DSD512 and two inputs that do DSD64, with nothing in between to explain the gap. Eighth occurrence of the missing network interface.
